situation: Korean DART filing asks for a quarter-only (3-month) consolidated operating profit in 억원 from a half-year or quarterly report. The income statement gives both 3-month and cumulative columns in 천원, and the figure is a loss shown with parentheses or a minus sign. Before the edit, the agent stored the value without its sign or label, then looped on the same compute and never submitted a final answer.
lesson: When pulling a figure from a DART income statement, record the line label, the period column (3-month vs cumulative) and the sign (parentheses or 손실 mean negative) in the upserted evidence. Convert 천원 to 억원 by dividing by 100,000, round as asked, and submit the final answer as soon as the compute succeeds instead of recomputing the same expression.

ops.content: Period columns: 반기보고서/분기보고서 income statements show both a 3-month column (3개월) and a cumulative column (누적). For a single-quarter question (e.g. 2분기 4~6월), copy the 3-month column of the 당기 period, not 누적 and not 전기. Final basis: if list_docs shows a [정정] filing or a later filing for the same period, use it instead of the original or a preliminary (잠정) figure. Check the unit line of the same table before converting (천원 → 억원 divide by 100,000; 백만원 → 억원 divide by 100), then round as asked.

Never repeat an identical compute; a repeated result means it is time to answer.

situation: A Korean DART financial-figure question asks for the 'final confirmed' (최종 확정) consolidated amount in a stated unit. Several filings exist for the same fiscal year, including a correction ([기재정정]). Without guidance, the agent reads the original report once and then repeats identical searches for the corrected filing, never reading or recording anything.
lesson: For DART figure questions, list the company's filings first, pick the latest correction for the target period, read the relevant section, and upsert the figure with its unit before converting units with compute. A final answer can only cite evidence ids that were already admitted, so record the figure before trying to finalize rather than retrying compute or final with an id that does not exist yet.

situation: A DART-style filing question asks for one consolidated figure, such as net income, in a target unit like 억원 at a stated precision. The filing reports the figure in a different unit (e.g. 백만원). Without a recipe, the agent re-searched and re-read the same document. It then called compute on an evidence id it had never created, and it ran out of turns without a final answer.
lesson: Once the consolidated statement row is found, first upsert the exact reported value and its unit as evidence, citing the read span. Then compute the unit conversion (백만원→억원 = ÷100) from that evidence id, and finalize with the requested precision. Never reference an evidence id in compute before upsert has admitted it, and stop searching once the figure has been read.

ops.content:

situation: A growth-rate question needs two figures (current and prior year) from one filing. The agent read the right section but kept re-running the identical search instead of extracting both figures. It saved only one value and never computed or finalized.
lesson: Block exact-repeat searches with a message telling the agent to read or extract from results it already has. Require derived answers to go through a compute step over recorded evidence. Together these push the agent to save both year values from passages already read, compute the ratio and finalize, instead of looping on search.

ops.content: Evidence discipline: right after any read that shows a needed value, upsert it (value + unit + period, citing that span) before doing anything else. Never repeat an identical search; if a search already pointed you to a document, read further offsets in it instead. For derived answers (growth %, ratio, difference), first list every input (e.g. current AND prior period from the same table) in unresolved, upsert each one, then compute from the evidence ids and finalize. Leave at least 3 turns for upsert, compute and final.

situation: The agent has already found the right annual report but cannot pin down the consolidated income-statement figure. It keeps re-issuing the same search query and paging through the document chunk by chunk, never records evidence, and runs out of turns with no answer.
lesson: Block exact-repeat searches and tell the agent to target the summary financial-data section, record the figure as evidence as soon as it is read, and then convert and finalize with that evidence cited. This turns a search loop into a short read-upsert-compute-final path. Truncating to the stated decimal place (rather than rounding) should be checked separately against the answer convention.

ops.content: Evidence and coverage discipline: right after every read, upsert any value that bears on the question, citing that span, before taking another action. Do not repeat a search you already ran. Once the figure is upserted, compute if needed and then finalize.
